answers.answer: Start with 25 money; 1 active association worker and 3 inactive; draw 8 Zoo cards and keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I, with Animals in the leftmost (strength 1) slot and the other four randomly placed. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for second, 2 for third, and 3 for fourth.
answers.evidence: Personal setup: ‘Place 1 association worker ... (the active worker) and the remaining 3’; ‘Take 25 money’; ‘Draw 2 Final Scoring cards’; ‘Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4’; Animals is under the leftmost slot; C1 gives the turn-order appeal stagger.

answers.answer: For 2 players, place 3 face-up Base Conservation Projects and block the left level on the left card, middle level on the middle card, and right level on the right card; also block the three left-column donation spaces. For 3 players, place 3 face-up base projects and there are no stated blocked spaces. For 4 players, place 4 face-up base projects and there are no stated blocked spaces. Reveal the initial 6-card display after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b: ‘In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up ...; otherwise the 3 topmost.’ Setup 5c specifies the 2-player blocked levels and donation spaces. Setup G: ‘After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.’

answers.answer: After using a card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, and place the used card in slot 1. Set strength before performing the action; each X-token spent adds +1 strength, any number may be spent, and X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. The holding limit is 5 X-tokens. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect after completing the action and moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the used card, shift cards left of the empty slot right, and put the used card in slot 1; strength is set ‘before’ the action; max 5 X-tokens; ‘After finishing’ waits until after moving the Action cards.

answers.answer: No: you may not do nothing, and playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal regular action. Instead, select an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right. Its slot strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot take this action if you already have 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says ‘You may not do nothing’; X-token action: ‘take exactly 1 X-token,’ still select and move a card to slot 1, with strength and upgrade irrelevant; unavailable at 5 X-tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement beyond that space and gain 1 X-token for reaching it. Finish the current turn; the break happens after it, then play continues clockwise with the next player after the break and the Break token reset to its starting space.
answers.evidence: Break track: ‘the break takes place after the end of your current turn’; you get ‘1 X-token’; ‘Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space’; after the break play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: Both sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. On side I, choose either a deck draw using the strength table (up to 3 cards, with any required discard) or a snap at strength 5+: take exactly 1 display card of any reputation, with no deck draw. On side II, draw from the deck and/or from display cards within reputation range, in any order, using the upgraded table; alternatively snap at strength 3+, taking exactly 1 display card of any reputation and no deck draw. The reputation restriction applies to side-II display draws, not snaps. Refill the display after the turn, and enforce the hand limit only at breaks.
answers.evidence: Cards action: each side advances the Break token 2 spaces; side I offers draw or snap at 5+; side II offers deck/range draws or snap at 3; either snap is one card of any reputation; display refills at turn end; discard to hand limit during breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. At space 15, each further reputation step gives 1 appeal while the counter remains at 15. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track: ‘Within reputation range’ means the matching folder and all lower-numbered folders; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 each further step gives 1 appeal; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than strength. Build II can build multiple different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in that action. Each costs 2 money per space, paid before placement. The first building must include at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces and not on water or rock; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Each kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately increases appeal by 1, once.
answers.evidence: Build action states exact I/II limits, cost ‘2 money per space,’ first-building border rule, later adjacency, water/rock and restricted-space limits, kiosk spacing, and immediate +1 appeal per pavilion.

answers.answer: Build I offers standard enclosures (sizes 1–5) and a size-3 Petting Zoo; it also offers kiosks and pavilions. Build II additionally offers the size-5 Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary. There are 4 of each special-enclosure tile in the components, while each zoo may build at most 1 Petting Zoo, 1 Reptile House, and 1 Large Bird Aviary. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Components list ‘4× Petting Zoo, 4× Reptile House, 4× Large Bird Aviary.’ Build I and II list their available enclosures and per-zoo maximums; unique buildings ‘only come into play via their Sponsor cards’; full map grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps; Association II also allows workers or bonuses gained from an earlier task to be used later in that action. Resolve items one at a time and pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefits. Immediate placement/play effects resolve during the action; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until after the action and Action-card movement. When effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: earlier bonuses may be used for later steps, items resolve one at a time, and each item is paid before its own benefits. Association II allows earlier-task gains to be used later. ‘After finishing’ and simultaneous-effect rules specify their timing/order.

answers.answer: For each animal, check all conditions, pay its cost, house it legally, place its card, then resolve effects. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon on the card, including a double icon; you must be able to pay the full cost before play effects pay money back. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the required size; flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side and it normally houses one animal. Some animals also require adjacency to one or two distinct water/rock hexes; repeated edges to the same terrain hex count once. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may use their shown special enclosure alternative, occupying the indicated number of spaces with supply player tokens; special enclosures are never flipped. Ordinary effects resolve immediately (including between animals), while ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action and card movement are done; the player chooses the order of simultaneous effects.
answers.evidence: Animals action gives the sequence and partner discount ‘3 money per continent icon’; standard enclosures flip, special enclosures use tokens and never flip; terrain counts distinct adjacent hexes; and it specifies immediate versus after-finishing effect timing.

answers.answer: Animals II permits display animals within reputation range, with an additional cost equal to the card's folder number; animals may be any mix from hand and display, and the display is not replenished until the turn ends. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to that action. Animals II also permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals II: display cards within reputation range cost the folder number; hand/display can be mixed and display refills at turn end; at strength 5+ reputation increases ‘at the very beginning’; upgrade-required animal conditions are allowed.

answers.answer: Existing animals may move into a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary only immediately when that building is built, once per building. The summary says suitable animals may move; reptiles and some birds are shown as eligible for the corresponding special-enclosure alternative. Each moved animal uses the number of special-enclosure spaces indicated on its card, marked with that many supply player tokens. For each animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain; if none does, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none. The summary does not state a fixed maximum number of animals to move beyond suitable animals and available special-enclosure space.
answers.evidence: Build II permits moving suitable animals ‘immediately — and only once per building’; animal rules say reptiles and some birds can use special enclosures and mark the indicated spaces with tokens. Special Rules give the standard-enclosure fallback sequence. No fixed total number of transferable animals is stated.

answers.answer: The task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total value is at most the action strength. Each task requires an active worker. If one of your workers is already on a task, you need to place 2 workers to repeat it; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot do it again before the break. Other players' workers on that task do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association action lists the four task values and I/II limits; it specifies one worker, two workers when one of yours is already there, prohibition when three of yours are there, and that other players' workers do not matter.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from the Association board and place them in the lowest available space in the corresponding column on your map; take printed bonuses immediately. The board tiles are replenished at breaks so each is available exactly once, skipping ones all players already have. Partner zoos must be from different continents and are limited to 4; a third or fourth requires Association II. Duplicate universities are not allowed. A university with its printed reputation bonus advances reputation, and universities grant research icons; a particular university raises the break-time hand limit from 3 to 5.
answers.evidence: Association tasks take tiles from the board to the lowest available map space and grant printed bonuses; duplicate continents/universities are forbidden; break setup replenishes availability; the summary states partner and hand-limit restrictions.

answers.answer: Association I project work can support a project already in play, or play a project card from hand and support it immediately. Association II can also play a new project from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number. Support a condition that has no token on it and that you fulfill; put one chosen token from the left edge of your zoo map on it. Each player may support a given project only once. Removing the map token activates its bonus immediately, and some bonuses also pay in each break; choose whether to take that bonus before or after the project reward. Above-board project capacity is 2, 3, or 4 according to player count; if a new project exceeds it, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to their owners' supplies, while already activated map bonuses stay activated. Base projects stay below the board and are never moved.
answers.evidence: Association project work states entry routes, support conditions and once-per-project limit, map-token source, reward/bonus timing, player-count display limits, overflow discard/token return, and base-project handling.

answers.answer: Yes. The animal's printed standard-enclosure size must match the release project's depicted size exactly, even if it could also use a special enclosure. On release, lose only that animal's printed appeal before gaining conservation; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. To free space, first remove its special-enclosure tokens if it could live in a special enclosure and enough tokens are present; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, or if none does, the smallest occupied enclosure meeting size alone; if none meets even size, flip none. Playing a new release project gives 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
answers.evidence: Release-into-the-wild rules specify exact standard size, loss/retention, special-token-first handling, standard-enclosure fallback, and the reputation for playing versus supporting an existing project.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II plays one or more from hand and/or the display within reputation range, paying the folder number for each display card; strength +1 must be at least the sum of levels. Resolve cards one at a time, fully resolving instant effects except ‘after finishing’ effects before the next card. Alternatively, the money option advances the Break token by the action strength and pays that much money on side I; side II pays twice that money. Side I pays the full strength amount even if fewer steps remain before the break space.
answers.evidence: Sponsors action gives I and II level budgets, card sources and folder cost, sequential resolution, and break-track money options; side I states full money even if the Break token needs fewer steps.

answers.answer: Break order: discard to the hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the particular university); return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, shift remaining cards down, and refill; take income; then reset the Break token. Each kiosk earns 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, while empty special enclosures do. Income is appeal-based money, then kiosk income, then break-income icons on Sponsors and activated map bonuses. When multiple players take display cards during income, refill after each player; if effects require an order, start with the break initiator (or the affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Break procedure lists the steps and income order; kiosk rules list qualifying neighbors and empty-enclosure exceptions; it says to refill the display after each player taking display cards during income and gives the order if effects require it.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token at that space. The first player to reach or exceed 10 makes all players discard one Final Scoring card. Check the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when your Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or pass one another; appeal gained during another player's turn waits until the end of your turn or a break unless another player triggers the end first. The triggering player completes their turn and everyone else gets one final turn; if triggered during a break, every player gets one final turn. If nobody reaches 10 conservation, discard one Final Scoring card before scoring. Each Final Scoring card can award at most 4 conservation points. Victory Points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area of your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with most conservation-project supports, then a shared victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions gives the rewards at 2, 5, 8, and 10; end-check timing and other-player-turn appeal; last turns; no-10 discard; 4-point cap; VP formula and tiebreak.
